steps.name: S6: OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY setting for the review app's scan limiter
steps.description: The memory gate's fail path says 'lower the review-app scan concurrency to 1', but no setting exists: the limit is the literal CONCURRENT_SCANS = 2 (crates/review-domain/src/budget.rs:30, used at :71) and the root builds ScanLimiter::default() (crates/openlore-review-app/src/wiring.rs:578). Add OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY: unset = 2 (today's value), a whole number in 1..=4 accepted, anything else (0, 5, blank-after-trim handled as unset like other vars, signed, decimal, suffixed, overflow) refused at startup with ConfigError::OutOfRange naming the variable and the range. Thread the value into the pure budget decision and the limiter; set it explicitly in deploy/review-app/host/compose.yaml; document it.
criteria: With OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY unset, the parsed config carries a scan concurrency of 2 and the app admits at most 2 concurrent scans (unchanged behaviour).

For every decimal u64 n, the setting is accepted as n exactly when 1 <= n <= 4; otherwise the config is refused with OutOfRange { name: "OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY", value: <given>, range: 1..=4 }.
Any text containing a non-digit character (other than a leading '+', matching DuckDbCap::parse semantics) is refused.

For every limit L in 1..=4 and every sequence of start/finish steps over 4 DIDs, the number of running scans never exceeds L, and a start is answered AppBusy exactly when L scans are running and the DID is otherwise admissible.
With L = 2 the budget's admissions are identical, step for step, to today's behaviour (regression guard for the default).
The review app binary refuses to start (non-zero exit, error names the variable) when OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY=0 or 5, and starts with 1.
deploy/review-app/host/compose.yaml sets OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY: "2" and the compose cap test asserts that literal.
The variable is documented where the review app's other caps are (deploy/README.md review-app section, devops platform-architecture/infrastructure-integration env table).
scenario_fns: crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs::tests::a_scan_concurrency_is_accepted_exactly_within_its_range (proptest; universe = every u64 in decimal x unset; literal oracle 1..=4, default 2)
crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs::tests::text_with_a_non_digit_is_never_a_scan_concurrency (proptest)

crates/review-domain/src/budget.rs::tests::running_scans_never_exceed_the_configured_concurrency (proptest; L in 1..=4 literal, step sequences over 4 DIDs; state-delta: running-set size before/after each step)
crates/review-domain/src/budget.rs::tests::a_limit_of_two_admits_exactly_as_before (proptest; compares against a literal-2 reference model written in the test, not CONCURRENT_SCANS)
tests/acceptance/review_app_resource_caps.rs::the_review_app_refuses_a_scan_concurrency_outside_its_range (integration, single-example: 0 and 5 refused, 1 accepted)
xtask/tests/indexer_deployment_platform.rs::the_review_app_container_is_capped_for_sharing_the_host (extend: OPENLORE_REVIEW_SCAN_CONCURRENCY == "2")

steps.implementation_notes:
TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): Unit tests for this step MUST be written as property-based tests using proptest strategies + state-delta assertions over a declared universe. Single-example unit tests are FALLBACK only — document why in a `// bypass:` comment if used. Acceptance scenarios are framed as properties where the contract supports it; classic scenarios are fallback. Integration and E2E tests REMAIN single-example — they verify wiring, not invariants.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first).
RED first: write all scenario_fns, run test_command, record the failure (compile error on the missing field/parameter counts as RED for new API; the compose assertion and the integration refusal must fail by assertion).
Design (WHAT, crafter owns HOW): contract shapes — parse_config stays pure-function (env map -> Result<AppConfig, ConfigError>); admit_scan stays pure-function with the limit as an explicit input (parameter or a field of ScanBudget; choose one, keep release_scan unchanged); ScanLimiter is bounded-change (only its own Mutex<ScanBudget>). The composition root builds the limiter from config.scan_concurrency instead of ScanLimiter::default(). Keep CONCURRENT_SCANS as the documented default (or rename to DEFAULT_CONCURRENT_SCANS) so call sites and docs stay truthful.
Validation style: mirror db_cap (config.rs:176-189) and DuckDbCap::parse (crates/ports/src/duckdb_caps.rs:29-35): whole decimal, no inner trimming beyond the shared `get` trim, range check, OutOfRange carries name/value/range. Do NOT add a variant to ports::DuckDbCap: scan concurrency is not a DuckDB cap and has a single consumer (rejected alternative: shared ports module — adds a cross-crate dependency for one app; rejected alternative: unvalidated usize parse — fails open on 0, which would deadlock every scan as AppBusy).
Oracles: literal values only (1..=4, default 2, the literal variable name). Never call or mirror production code in an oracle: do not reference CONCURRENT_SCANS, DuckDbCap::range or the new constant from the test's expected side. Note the existing budget.rs:159 assertion uses CONCURRENT_SCANS as oracle — switch it to the literal while touching the file.
LESSONS: oracles use literal values, never call/mirror production code; run dependent suites narrowly (the test_command above, not the workspace); deploy/** is checked by deploy-pds-check (compose resolve + mount guard) so keep compose valid; no AWS/tofu actions.
Mutation scope (per-feature, >= 80%): budget.rs admit_scan, config.rs scan-concurrency parse, wiring line.

steps.name: S7 + N3 (+N4): review-app deploy.sh install fails closed like the indexer
steps.description: deploy/review-app/deploy.sh host_install (176-188) has no IMDS isolation check, no check that Caddy actually imports the sites directory, creates /pds/caddy/sites itself (:179, defeating the indexer's existence check at deploy/indexer/deploy.sh:355) and reloads Caddy without validating (:186). Make it fail closed: run the same refuse_unless_isolated contract as the indexer (digest-pinned curlimages/curl probe on pds_default; positive control first; only curl exit 7/28 proves isolation), refuse unless the Caddy container sees /etc/caddy/sites and /etc/caddy/Caddyfile imports /etc/caddy/sites/*.caddy, never create /pds/caddy/sites, run `caddy validate` before reload and remove app.caddy if it is rejected. N4 if cheap: the indexer's first-deploy readiness wait (60 s) is overridable for the first deploy that includes certificate issuance.
criteria: host install proceeds only when the probe's positive control (curl --version on pds_default) succeeds AND the IMDS PUT ends with curl exit 7 or 28.
IMDS exit 0, 22, 6, 125, a failed positive control, or a probe image not pinned by @sha256:<64 hex> each refuse with a message containing 'refusing' and a non-zero exit, before any `install` call.

MANDATORY in BOTH scripts (same shared function text, same SITES variable): (a) `docker inspect` of the PDS Caddy container shows a mount with Source == "$SITES" (host /pds/caddy/sites) AND Destination == /etc/caddy/sites, else refuse; a mount with the right destination but any other source refuses.

MANDATORY in BOTH scripts: (b) the Caddyfile read from inside the Caddy container matches the anchored regex `^[[:space:]]*import[[:space:]]+/etc/caddy/sites/\*\.caddy` on some line, else refuse; a commented `# import /etc/caddy/sites/*.caddy` (or the import inside any other text on the line) refuses. Checks (a) and (b) run before any host file is written; the message points at tofu-aws-pds v1.7.0 / R-REPLACE.

MANDATORY in BOTH scripts: (c) after the site file (app.caddy / index.caddy) is placed, `caddy adapt --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` output must contain the app's host (app.<PDS_HOSTNAME> / index.<PDS_HOSTNAME>); if it does not, the site file is removed, Caddy is NOT reloaded, and the install refuses.

`host deploy` and `host redeploy` with a failed isolation/sites check record NO render-secrets, NO docker pull, NO stop (compose stop/down) and NO compose up: the running app is untouched (both call host_install first; review-app deploy.sh:233 and :290).
No code path of deploy/review-app/deploy.sh creates /pds/caddy/sites (no install -d / mkdir naming it); a missing sites directory refuses.
`caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` runs after app.caddy is placed and before `caddy reload`; on validate failure app.caddy is removed, reload is NOT called, and install exits non-zero.
The isolation function in both deploy.sh scripts is behaviourally identical (same probe image digest, same exit-code table); a drift between them fails a test.
Both deploy/review-app and deploy/indexer scripts stay `bash -n` clean and `shellcheck -S info` clean.

(N4, optional) the indexer's ready wait is overridable for the first deploy (default unchanged at 60 s) and the override is covered by a test; if skipped, 01-03's checklist documents the certificate-issuance wait.

steps.implementation_notes:
EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: shell/doc artefact; compensate with xtask tests.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first): every refusal test asserts the recorded-calls log (the state delta of the host) contains no `install`, no `caddy reload`, and no write to the sites dir.
RED first: write all scenario_fns and show them failing against today's deploy/review-app/deploy.sh (today install runs `install -d ... /pds/caddy/sites` with no probe, so every refusal assertion fails).
Pattern to follow: refuse_unless_isolated + imds_probe + IMDS_PROBE_IMAGE (deploy/indexer/deploy.sh:339-367) and its tests host_install_with_probe / the_imds_probe_accepts_only_a_proven_unreachable_metadata_service (xtask/tests/indexer_deployment_platform.rs:1383-1500). Reuse decision: each deploy.sh is shipped to the host as a self-contained payload (review-app :96, indexer :121 copy deploy.sh itself), and deploy-pds-check shellchecks only deploy/review-app and deploy/indexer, so copy the function verbatim into the review-app script and guard drift with both_apps_refuse_with_the_same_isolation_contract. Rejected alternative: a sourced deploy/lib/isolation.sh — needs both payload copies, both shellcheck globs and the SSM runner to agree; more moving parts for ~20 lines. If the crafter prefers the shared file anyway, add it to both payload cp lines and both shellcheck steps in .github/workflows/deploy-pds-check.yml.
Test seam: add REVIEW_APP_CADDY_SITES_DIR (default /pds/caddy/sites) mirroring INDEXER_CADDY_SITES_DIR so tests point at a temp dir. Sites-hook checks are MANDATORY and live in the shared isolation/readiness function, byte-identical in both scripts and keyed on the same variable name SITES (review app: SITES="${REVIEW_APP_CADDY_SITES_DIR:-/pds/caddy/sites}"; indexer keeps INDEXER_CADDY_SITES_DIR) so both_apps_refuse_with_the_same_isolation_contract holds: (a) `docker inspect` the PDS Caddy container's Mounts; require one entry with Source == "$SITES" and Destination == /etc/caddy/sites (a destination match alone is foolable); (b) read /etc/caddy/Caddyfile from inside the container and require the anchored regex ^[[:space:]]*import[[:space:]]+/etc/caddy/sites/\*\.caddy (grep -E), so a commented import fails; (c) a second shared function, called after the site file is placed with the expected host as argument, runs `caddy adapt --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` and requires the host in its output, else removes the file and refuses; then validate, then reload. The indexer's existing tests' docker stub must answer inspect/cat/adapt (update host_install_with_probe), and its existing behaviour stays green. host_deploy/host_redeploy call host_install first (review-app :233/:290, indexer :434/:496), so the guard covers them; the untouched-app scenario proves the ordering cannot regress.
CI stubs must be able to FAIL: every stub (docker, caddy via docker, install) must have a configurable non-zero branch exercised by at least one test; a stub that always succeeds hid a gap last time. Assert on recorded calls, not only on exit codes.
Oracles: literal values (exit codes 7/28 vs 0/22/6/125, the literal digest prefix curlimages/curl@sha256:, literal paths). No production function is called from the expected side.
LESSONS: deploy/** is checked by deploy-pds-check (shellcheck stricter than local: run shellcheck -S info locally); run dependent suites narrowly; no AWS/tofu actions; never run the scripts against a real host.
Contract shape: host_install is unbounded-preservation until the probe passes (refusal = zero host mutations), then bounded-change (APP dirs, app.caddy, timer).

steps.implementation_notes:
EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: shell/doc artefact; compensate with xtask tests. Exception: the drift scanner's own self-test (the_drift_scanner_flags_literal_drift_fixtures) is a proptest over generated markdown, since the scanner is a pure text function.
STAGE CONTEXT: bug-prone legacy code = Stage 1 (state-delta capture of hidden mutations first).
RED first (mandatory evidence): write go_live_runbook_drift.rs BEFORE editing any doc, run `cargo test -p xtask --test go_live_runbook_drift`, and record the failure output showing at least /admin/test-alarm (monitoring-alerting.md:132,133; kpi-instrumentation.md:92) and the plain plan at bluesky-claim-review-app/devops/infrastructure-integration.md:258. Only then fix the docs.
Scanner scope (universe): deploy/**/*.md excluding deploy/tofu/**/.terraform/**; docs/feature/bluesky-claim-review-app/devops/*.md; docs/feature/indexer-deployment/devops/*.md; docs/evolution/indexer-deployment-evolution.md (its sequence is in S3).
Code-side truth (read as text, not executed): admin routes = the (METHOD, "/admin/...") literals in crates/openlore-review-app/src/admin.rs route table (today /admin/kpi, /admin/purge); deploy.sh modes = the arms of the top-level `case "$cmd"` and `host_main` in each deploy.sh (split on `|`); OPENLORE_* settings = names that appear as literals in crates/**/src/**/*.rs, deploy/**/*.sh, deploy/**/compose.yaml or deploy/tofu/**/*.tf (excluding .terraform) — never in *.md, so a doc cannot vouch for itself.
Matching rules (avoid false positives): admin = regex `/admin/[a-z-]+`; modes = `deploy\.sh[ \t]+([a-z][a-z-]*)` inside code spans/fences, checked against that app's script when the path is qualified (deploy/indexer/ vs deploy/review-app/) or the doc lives under that app's folder, else against the union; also expand `install | redeploy | stop` lists; setting = `OPENLORE_[A-Z0-9_]+`. Replacement plan = a line containing `tofu plan` and `-out=` whose contiguous block (until a blank line or fence end) contains `OPENLORE_ALLOW_DELETE=1`, or which sits under a heading containing `R-REPLACE`; it must contain `-replace=`. Verified negatives to keep passing: deploy/README.md:97 (normal prod plan, no ALLOW_DELETE=1 in its block), deploy/README.md:142 (has -replace=), indexer-deployment infrastructure-integration.md:367 (says 'without OPENLORE_ALLOW_DELETE'), infrastructure-integration.md:276 (`tofu plan` with no -out). Each finding prints file:line and the token.
Checklist content (WHAT): step 0 v1.7.0 released + `git ls-remote --tags` check; bump both roots together; verified identity backup; R-REPLACE with `-replace=module.pds.aws_instance.pds` and `OPENLORE_ALLOW_DELETE=1 check-plan.sh` (rollback first: stop both apps, then re-pin v1.6.0 with -replace=); post-replace verification; bootstrap + prod applies once (review-app.tf and indexer.tf, alarms disabled); SSM secrets; GHCR public + anonymous pull check per image; DID list; review-app deploy, indexer deploy (first-deploy wait includes certificate issuance); rollback drills; memory gate; confirm SNS subscription; enable alarms (apply); THEN test-fire A-1/A-3/A-7/A-8 and A1/A2/A3; REVIEW_APP_LIVE; announce. Keep operator decisions as explicit decision points, not choices made.
Memory gate: loop such as `for i in $(seq 240); do ... cat "$cg/memory.peak"; grep MemAvailable /proc/meminfo; sleep 5; done` (crafter writes the exact text); cgroup path per container id; search body inline (e.g. a heredoc with a literal query object); load generator paced under 10/s with burst < 50 (e.g. `xargs -P 4` with a per-request sleep, or count 429 as expected). Verify the request shape against the searchClaims handler before writing it.
S9: compose mem_limit is 192m (deploy/review-app/host/compose.yaml:24). Prefer fixing the wave-decisions R-3 text over adding an anonymous-pull check to deploy.sh (not cheap: needs an unauthenticated registry call path); record the dated correction inline, do not rewrite history.
LESSONS: oracles use literal values, never call/mirror production code (the self-test fixtures and threshold assertions are literal strings; the real-doc checks read code as TEXT, never link the crates); CI stubs must be able to FAIL (the scanner self-test injects drift and asserts it is caught); run dependent suites narrowly; deploy/** is checked by deploy-pds-check (any shell snippet added under deploy/ must pass shellcheck -S info if it is a .sh file); no AWS/tofu actions — commands are written, never run.
